rule.description: A struct type with at least 8 own methods is a god class when the callables that own it — its own methods plus free functions that take the class as their leading operand (disguised methods) — span at least 2 qualified build-pipeline concern domains, with each domain contributing its own minimum number of the class's callables: at least 2 callables anchored in go/ast or go/parser source surgery (signatures carrying go/ast or go/parser types, or bodies driving that machinery), at least 1 callable driving the goembed expander for embedded-asset synthesis, and at least 2 callables constructing *PackageData package-descriptor variants. Consolidation is a property of class ownership, not of the syntactic form its callables take: re-spelling a method as a function that threads the class as a leading parameter does not free the class of the concern.

checks.description: The native overlay augmentation pipeline — the code surgery that parses original and overlaid Go sources, rewrites import declarations, applies override declarations, prunes imports, and finalizes removals — is owned by Session methods instead of a dedicated pipeline collaborator. In the pinned clean revision these callables are free functions parameterized by the build context they need; the injection pulls them onto the Session receiver and threads their per-package bookkeeping through Session fields (augOverrides, augFound), so Session's own method set comes to span go/ast and go/parser machinery it previously delegated.
checks.detected_relation: class (>= 8 own methods) -> >= 2 of its callables anchored in go/ast or go/parser source surgery, absorbed from the pipeline's dedicated stage
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Session, the type that drives the overall build, now also implements the source-surgery stage end to end, mixing parse-tree rewriting concerns into the orchestrator that should only coordinate them.

matches.evidence: Augment.go line 82: the sweep that parses overlay and original sources per package became a Session method whose signature carries *token.FileSet and whose body drives go/parser over overlay and original sources; it resets the per-package bookkeeping stored in the Session fields augOverrides and augFound on every call and dispatches the session-owned override-verification step (checkOverrides) that validates overridden identifiers against that bookkeeping.
Augment.go line 121: parses the native overlay sources through go/parser with werr-driven syntax error collection; signature carries []*ast.File results.
Augment.go line 165: parses the package's original source files via go/parser, threading the session's environment through to control the parser context.
Augment.go line 209: rewrites an overlay *ast.File's declarations in place, splitting and rewriting type declarations via go/ast node surgery.
Augment.go line 268: rewrites an original file's go/ast import declarations to apply arch-tagged import selection to ordinary imports.

Augment.go line 292: applies the overlay's override declarations (gopherjs:new, gopherjs:purge, and gopherjs:override-signature directives) to an original *ast.File, recording which named types the overrides actually matched into the Session field augFound.
Augment.go line 419: walks a parsed *ast.File's declarations and imports to decide whether the file carries nothing but imports.
Augment.go line 447: prunes unused go/ast import declarations from a rewritten file after overlay application removed their usages.
Augment.go line 520: finalizes deferred *ast.File decl removal by erasing the declarations that decided removal during augmentation.

Embed.go line 35: the embedded-asset synthesis callable became a Session method; it also anchors the source-surgery domain because it feeds synthesized sources through go/ast construction and go/parser.ParseFile before returning the file.

Build.go line 385: a pre-existing Session method whose dominance in go/ast- and go/parser-anchored orchestration drags the Session class over the consolidation threshold only once the injection has absorbed the other source-surgery callables into the same class; this match is credited to the class-level entry because the method was not moved by the injection, the class was.

checks.description: The goembed-driven synthesis of embedded-asset initializers — resolving embed patterns, building the embedded filesystem tables, and emitting the generated js_embed.go source — became a Session method, so the task of generating synthetic source for a package's embedded assets is owned by the build-session orchestrator.
checks.detected_relation: class (>= 8 own methods) -> >= 1 of its callables anchoring the goembed expander machinery
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Embedded-asset synthesis is a self-contained pipeline stage with its own library machinery; owning it on Session couples the orchestrator to the code-generation stage it should merely invoke.

matches.evidence: Embed.go line 35: drives goembed.CheckEmbed, goembed.NewResolve, goembed.BuildFS, and goembed.BytesToHex to synthesize the initializer file for the package's go:embed variables; in the pinned clean revision this is a package-level callable that takes the package descriptor, not a Session method.

checks.description: Constructing package-descriptor variants — the in-package test variant, the external (black-box) test variant, and the ad-hoc ephemeral package assembled for a synthetic tooling target — moved from the PackageData type itself (and from inline assembly inside the per-package build flow) onto Session methods, so the descriptor's own lifecycle logic is now driven through the session receiver. The absorbed metadata cluster also includes the descriptor's file-modification-time lookup and installed-archive path resolution (FileModTime, InstallPath), which share the same mistaken ownership even though they carry no domain anchor that this rule counts.
checks.detected_relation: class (>= 8 own methods) -> >= 2 of its callables constructing *PackageData package-descriptor variants
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Package-descriptor variants describe the package, not the session; when the session receiver constructs them, every caller must route through the session, dragging descriptor lifecycle knowledge into the orchestrator.

matches.evidence: Pkgmeta.go line 18: builds the in-package test variant as a new &PackageData{...} composite literal carrying the test-tagged build context, re-owned from the PackageData value receiver that held it in the pinned clean revision.
Pkgmeta.go line 35: builds the external test variant as a new &PackageData{...} composite literal with the xtest tag applied, re-owned from the PackageData value receiver.

Pkgmeta.go line 122: fabricates an ephemeral ad-hoc package descriptor — forcing artificial build attributes, patched dummy time, and an &PackageData{...} composite literal — as a second construction site of package variants inlined into Session instead of remaining part of the per-package build flow.

excluded.reason: The compiler's context helper has 8+ own methods, but each of its methods serves a single concern domain — they walk, build, and emit compiled expressions for the target language rather than absorbing a second pipeline stage — so the multi-domain qualification never triggers; no threshold was tuned around this method-laden single-concern owner.

The package-descriptor struct stays below the 8-own-method gate (6 receiver methods after the injection strips its variant methods away), and in the repaired state its free helpers (embedFiles, parserOriginalFiles) remain free functions; the class-level method-count gate keeps the descriptor itself outside the rule in every state.

The pipeline owner implied by a sound repair legitimately holds 10 methods, but they all serve the single source-surgery domain, so the rule does not penalize a cohesive extracted owner; only concern-spanning consolidation matches.

These types are method-rich but uniformly anchored in a single concern domain (test-main synthesis and source collection respectively); they do not qualify under the multi-domain rule in any analyzed state.
